**English methodological description (not translated)**

Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers approved this state primary education standard by Resolution No. 87 of 21 February 2018. It sets compulsory learning outcomes and competency requirements for grades 1–4 across integrated educational fields and informs school-level educational programmes. It must be applied according to the legally effective consolidated text and the cohort transition rules: Resolution No. 1810 of 26 December 2025 introduces a replacement for learners beginning primary education from 1 September 2028. This record identifies the 2018 standard for applicable cohorts, not a timeless or cross-national equivalent.

**English methodological description (not translated)**

Adopted by Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers in Resolution No. 898 of 30 September 2020, this binding basic secondary education standard describes competency-based expected results across educational fields and the framework for grades 5–9. It informs model curricula and school educational programmes, including progression toward upper secondary choices. Amendments in 2026 affect terminology and accessibility as well as other provisions; practitioners must consult the currently effective consolidated act and transitional dates. It is neither a subject-by-subject course catalogue nor proof of compliance by any Svitlo Course.

The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine adopted the specialised upper secondary education standard under Resolution No. 851 of 25 July 2024. It specifies common and profile-dependent learning outcomes, content areas and organisational requirements for the upper secondary pathway, including academic and vocational directions. Its implementation is phased, with broad rollout planned from September 2027 and some experimental provisions earlier; Resolution No. 1000 of August 2026 changed parts of the text. The record describes the statutory framework, not a claim that it is already uniformly delivered in every grade or school.

**English methodological description (not translated)**

The Common Core State Standards Initiative's 2010 mathematics framework describes grade-specific mathematics content and cross-grade Standards for Mathematical Practice for US kindergarten through high school. It emphasises conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, reasoning and modelling. These are state-led standards; states and districts decide adoption, revision and implementation, so the framework does not constitute a universal federal requirement. Local implementation may deviate from the original 2010 document and alignment must be evaluated against the applicable state's adopted version.

This 2010 state-led Common Core framework sets grade-banded expectations for reading, writing, speaking, listening and language across US K–12 schooling, with history/social studies, science and technical-subject literacy addressed specifically in secondary grades. The standards emphasise evidence from texts and disciplinary literacy; they do not replace the full curricula of the named subjects. Adoption and later modifications vary among US states. Neither the original initiative nor the presence of this reference establishes a nationally mandated syllabus or evidence of alignment for any course.

## Next Generation Science Standards

- UUID: `19e98cf2-3fc7-4d5c-9ddb-7d28388ab8cb`

- Canonical Code: [nextGenerationScienceStandards.data.ts](../../shared/education-standards/data/unitedStates/nextGenerationScienceStandards.data.ts)

**English methodological description (not translated)**

The Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS), released in April 2013, define K–12 science performance expectations integrating disciplinary core ideas, crosscutting concepts, and science and engineering practices. They provide a three-dimensional approach to learning and assessment in life, physical, and Earth/space sciences and engineering. NGSS were developed through a state-led process, and states adopt, adapt or decline them independently; they are not a US federal mandate. A Course's use of experiments or related vocabulary is not in itself evidence that all performance expectations are covered.

Poland's Minister of Education issued a new preschool core curriculum through the regulation of 11 March 2026, published in Dziennik Ustaw 2026 item 378 and later amended by item 958 of July 2026. Its preschool annex defines developmental and educational tasks, expected preparation for schooling, and cross-domain learning in early childhood settings. This record covers preschool only and is not a duplicate of the separate primary-school curriculum in the same regulation. Always check the amending act for the effective consolidated wording.

Länder determine curriculum implementation and assessments; they should be compared to the specific state curriculum when mapping a course.

**English methodological description (not translated)**

The Finnish National Agency for Education adopted the National Core Curriculum for Basic Education in 2014, providing the national foundation for the nine-year comprehensive school system, with progressive local implementation from 2016. It describes curricular values, transversal competencies, learning environments, assessment principles, grade-level subject objectives and support for learning. Education providers develop their own local curricula under this national framework; the 2014 title denotes the underlying core curriculum and does not exclude subsequent amendments, including provisions on learning support effective in August 2025. It is a nationally normative curriculum basis, not an unchanged 2014 classroom textbook.

## Varhaiskasvatussuunnitelman perusteet 2022

**English methodological description (not translated)**

The Finnish National Agency for Education's National Core Curriculum for Early Childhood Education and Care (2022) is a nationally binding framework for ECEC providers and settings. It describes pedagogical values, child participation, learning areas, assessment and cooperation with guardians, rather than subject-specific grade standards. Since 1 January 2025, providers have no legal duty to prepare a separate local ECEC curriculum, but they must implement the national core and prepare individual child ECEC plans. Amendments to the 2022 core took effect on 1 January and 1 August 2026. This record does not cover pre-primary education (esiopetus), which has its own core curriculum.

## Socle commun de connaissances, de compétences et de culture

**English methodological description (not translated)**

France's common foundation of knowledge, skills and culture is defined by the decree of 31 March 2015 and remains in force according to the Ministry of National Education while a proposed revision is being discussed. It specifies knowledge and competencies every pupil should acquire during compulsory schooling, grouped into broad domains such as language, learning methods, civic formation, natural and technical systems, and representations of the world. It frames national teaching programmes and cycle-based assessment; it is not itself a complete school curriculum or evidence of a course's accreditation. The 2025 draft revision must not be mistaken for enacted law.

**English methodological description (not translated)**

Estonia's Government Regulation No. 1 of 6 January 2011 establishes the national curriculum for basic schools (Põhikooli riiklik õppekava), defining the nine-year national basic-education standard. Its general part and subject-area annexes establish learning outcomes, transversal competencies, subject content, assessment principles and requirements for school curricula. Subsequent amendments include provisions with differing effective dates, notably changes published in December 2025, some taking effect in September 2026. Schools implement the national requirements through their own curricula; this record is not the distinct simplified basic-school curriculum or a secondary-school standard.
